items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Okay, what about the Jelly Roll Morton, then, now that we're talking about him? Where did you first meet him? [INTERVIEWEE] Right here.

ctx.x: What did they call him, then?
And what was he doing, then, or should I ask?
-- is all I can tell you about Jelly.
They said that Jelly copped it from somebody that most of them copy from him.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Jelly Roll -- Jelly Roll don't play like nobody else, he got his own style.

ctx.x: Did he influence any other players, other people play like in that style?
Do -- well I tell you, Jelly Roll -- Jelly Roll don't play like nobody else, he got his own style.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: We was gonna have an awful band. We had about ten or twelve of us... I was on the bass.

ctx.x: Or nothing. But Jelly used to just scrap up different players, you know. Oh. Pick up different man, the best he could, you see. I had a father named Willie Woodman who was playing trombone with him.
